by Tamara Nowakowsky
A residential building damaged in a Russian attack on Kharkiv, on Oct. 12, 2026. (State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Telegram)
Russian forces launched a large-scale missile attack on Kharkiv on Oct. 12, injuring at least 11 people, including an emergency responder, and damaging residential buildings across the city, according to Ukrainian authorities.
Three people trapped beneath the rubble were later rescued, UNIAN reported , citing Ukraine's State Emergency Service.
Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov said Russian forces had reportedly used 10 Banderol-type missiles in the attack, targeting civilian infrastructure.
In the city's Kholodnohirskyi district, a strike hit a four-story residential building, destroying an entire section. At least 10 nearby private houses were also damaged, Syniehubov said.

How would NATO defeat a Russian invasion? Its top commander envisions a wall of drones, a counteroffensive, and missile strikes deep behind Russian lines.
October 12, 2026, 4:07 pm
Source: The Wall Street Journal
Alexus Grynkewich at a forum in Warsaw, October 12, 2026
Omar Marques / Getty Images
General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said NATO forces would destroy “anything and everything” involved in any Russian attack on the alliance’s territory. He presented his “theory of victory” at a security conference in Warsaw.
Bloomberg reported a week earlier that Grynkewich would present a “quick victory” strategy for responding to a Russian advance on the alliance’s eastern flank. Reuters reported that he did not explicitly mention Russia in his speech, but his message was clearly directed at the Kremlin.
Grynkewich said NATO is a defensive alliance but will thwart, repel, and crush any attacks on its members:
If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight.…

titulekPuvodni: Russian diplomat expelled from Bulgaria in 2021 amid investigation into arms depot explosions now serves as assistant military attaché in Serbia, RFE/RL finds
shrnuti: RFE/RL’s Balkan Service and the investigative project Sistema have identified a diplomat at the Russian Embassy in Serbia who was declared persona non grata in Bulgaria in 2021 during an investigation into explosions at weapons depots.

Skip to main content
Russian diplomat expelled from Bulgaria in 2021 amid investigation into arms depot explosions now serves as assistant military attaché in Serbia, RFE/RL finds
October 12, 2026, 3:36 pm
Source: RFE/RL
RFE/RL’s Balkan Service and the investigative project Sistema have identified a diplomat at the Russian Embassy in Serbia who was declared persona non grata in Bulgaria in 2021 during an investigation into explosions at weapons depots.
Alexander Krasiy, an assistant military attaché, held the same position at the Russian Embassy in Bulgaria before moving to Serbia. In April 2021, Bulgaria’s Foreign Ministry said it was expelling a Russian diplomat but did not name him. The news agency Zona News and Bulgarian National Television identified him as Krasiy.
The decision came amid an investigation into explosions at four weapons depots and production facilities between 2011 and 2020. Bulgarian prosecutors suspected six Russians of involvement. According to prosecutors, the explosions may have been linked…

titulek: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
titulekPuvodni: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack
shrnuti: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

vyrez.text:
Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack - BBC News
Image source, AFP via Getty Images
By Ian Aikman
Published
1 hour ago
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
Hackers reportedly gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight.
The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.
More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while at least 300 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, according to the AFP news agency.
Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.
Some supermarket staff reportedly said they were hit by waves of hot air when they opened freezer units on Monday morning.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centres disrupt over 80 services | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo
Three consecutive Ukrainian drone attacks on data centres operated by Russian technology company Yandex have caused disruptions to more than 80 of its digital platforms and third-party but related services, such as banking apps and ride-hailing services. Bot traffic from the Yandex network has also fallen to almost zero.
Source : Tom's Hardware , citing Cloudflare data
Details : Tom's Hardware reported that on 8 October, when a Yandex data centre in Sasovo housing two supercomputers was damaged, bot traffic from the network fell to around 57% of its peak level. On 9 October, a larger Yandex data centre complex in Kaluga was put out of operation, followed by another facility in Vladimir on 11 October . As a result, bot traffic fell to 0.4% of the peak level recorded over the previous two weeks.

Podle prokuratury se pokusil o sebevraždu, ale pouze se zranil. Policisté rovněž zajistili jeho batoh, ve kterém do školy přinesl podomácku vyrobenou výbušninu, jež téměř explodovala.

Žák odborného učiliště v Ostrolence podle rádia RMF24  na spolužáky a pedagogy okolo jedenácté hodiny dopoledne během vyučování zaútočil mačetou. Konkrétně měl řádit ve čtvrtém ročníku školy.
Informace o počtu zraněných se přes den měnily. Mazovský vojvoda Mariusz Frankowski nakonec podle agentury PAP uvedl, že zraněných je deset lidí, včetně pachatele, pěti studentů, dvou učitelů…

shrnuti: Satellite images have revealed damage from a 25 September attack on Russia's Zavod Iskra plant in Ulyanovsk, which is involved in producing components for Kh-59 missiles.

vyrez.text:
Satellite images show damage to Russian plant producing Kh-59 missile components | Ukrainska Pravda
Satellite images have revealed the consequences of the 25 September attack on the Zavod Iskra research and production company in the Russian city of Ulyanovsk.
Source: OSINT analyst Dnipro Osint ⟨Harbuz⟩
Quote: "The images show that most of the strikes hit the building's façade rather than the roof. As a result, around 80% of the strikes were not captured by the satellite: only two of the 11 confirmed strikes caused visible damage in the imagery."
Advertisement:











Details: Dnipro OSINT believes the strikes on the façade could cause significantly more serious internal damage than hits on the roof, particularly if production facilities and equipment are located behind the walls.
Background: It was previously reported that Ukraine's defence forces had struck the Zavod Iskra in Ulyanovsk . Ukraine's General Staff said the facility is part of the Almaz-Antey concern and is involved in the production of Kh-59M2/M2A missiles and components for the 72V6 combat vehicle of the Pantsir-S1 air defence gun and missile system.

Germany arrests former domestic intelligence chief over alleged spying
August Hanning served as president of Federal Intelligence Service from 1998 to 2005
Germany’s federal prosecutor’s office has said a former domestic intelligence chief was arrested on Tuesday on espionage allegations.
August Hanning served as president of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from December 1998 to November 2005.
Hanning was arrested in Bad Toelz-Wolfratshausen, in southern Germany. A former aide of his, identified only as Manfred D, was also arrested on Tuesday.
The prosecutor’s office did not reveal who the men were suspected of spying for.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.
The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.
Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died.
Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea.

Moscow police detained around 60 people on Sunday during a Communist Party rally commemorating the 1993 constitutional crisis, after the event spiraled into a protest against alleged fraud during last month’s parliamentary elections.
An estimated 2,000 people gathered for an annual memorial honoring those killed during an Oct. 4, 1993, standoff when President Boris Yeltsin ordered tanks to shell the Supreme Soviet parliament building to dissolve opposition to his administration.

On Saturday, October 3rd, in Krāslava municipality, border guards—in cooperation with soldiers from the National Armed Forces—detained a Latvian citizen who was transporting individuals who had illegally crossed the state border, according to a State Border Guard release.

The plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo. Initial reports said six crew members were killed during a training flight from the Ukrainka air base.
A post about the unveiling of a memorial to the dead pilots later appeared on the “Rural News” community page for Seryshevo, a village in the Amur region where the Ukrainka air base is located. OSINT analyst duke garland noticed the post. Mediazona verified the information and found that all eight of those killed had served in strategic aviation.

October 5, 2026, 7:17 am
Source: Meduza
A bomb destroyed a car belonging to a participant in Russia’s war against Ukraine on October 2 in Novomoskovsk, in Russia’s Tula region, the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported.
The bomb had been planted under the car’s chassis, according to  data from the anonymous Russian Telegram channel VChK-OGPU. The driver killed was identified as Roman Syromyatnikov, and the Novomoskovsk-based news outlet Novomoskovsk Segodnya confirmed the death of a person by that name.
Syromyatnikov worked at Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) facilities in the Tula region during the 2010s. He signed a contract with Russia’s Defense Ministry in 2023 and returned to the Tula region for medical treatment in late 2024, the independent Russian investigative outlet iStories reported , citing leaked data.

Poland says Russian military helicopter violated its airspace
September 23, 2026, 3:04 pm
Source: Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces
A Russian military Mi-8 helicopter entered Polish airspace on September 23 at 11:08 a.m., the operational command of the Polish army said.
The helicopter, flying from the Kaliningrad region, crossed about 300 meters (984 feet) into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds, the Polish military said.
Poland scrambled fighter jets and put ground forces and equipment on alert. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense,” the command said.
Russia has not yet commented on the incident.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on September 17 that Russia is planning “hybrid” strikes using missiles and drones against countries that support Ukraine. He claimed that “there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles may fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank, even cause destruction.”

by Yuliia Taradiuk
Russia launched yet another drone attack against Kyiv on Oct. 12, hitting multiple districts of Ukraine's capital and injuring at least three people, city authorities said.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko first said at 11:32 a.m. local time that air defenses were operating in the city. Three people, including an elderly woman, were injured as a result of Russian drone attacks, he added.
Drone debris fell in an open area near residential buildings in the Solomyanskyi District of Kyiv and on a house in Darnytskyi District , while in the Pecherskyi District , a fire caused by wreckage of a drone that had crashed near a building was brought under control, Klitschko said.

Three injured in Russian drone attack on Kyiv | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo: Getty Images
Three people were injured in Kyiv in a Russian drone attack on 12 October. Drone debris fell on a house in the Darnytskyi district and near residential buildings in the Solomianskyi district.
Source : Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko
Quote : "The number of people injured in the capital has risen to three."
Advertisement:





Details : Drone debris fell on a house in the Darnytskyi district and on an open area near houses in the Solomianskyi district. Emergency services were dispatched to both locations.
Klitschko initially reported one person injured, who received medical assistance at the scene. He later reported another injured person, an elderly woman who was also treated at the scene. The number of injured subsequently rose to three.
Background : On 11 October, State Emergency Service bomb disposal experts removed a warhead and safe remnants of a ballistic missile from the site of one of the Russian strikes in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district.

After RAF Fairford incident, how big a threat to the UK is Iran?

Although there is scepticism about Tehran’s capabilities, it has become clear it wants Britain to feel it poses a risk
Britain may have been only peripherally involved in the bombing of Iran that Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu started, but in the past fortnight it has become clear that Tehran wants to pose a threat inside the UK in response.
In the aftermath of the confused incident near RAF Fairford, western officials are weighing up whether to warn publicly that Iran now has US military targets in Europe on its mind, such as the air force base in Gloucestershire.
That could come even though there remains British scepticism about Iran’s capability to pull off a drone raid on a secure facility far from Tehran.

Nejméně čtyři raněné si v noci na neděli vyžádal ruský útok na Dnipro na jihovýchodě Ukrajiny, uvedly úřady. Ukrajinské drony naopak podle médií napadly další datové centrum největší ruské technologické společnosti Yandex, tentokrát ve Vladimiru. Zprávy vycházejí z vyjádření společnosti, které citovala i ruská státní agentura TASS. Datové centrum je údajně zcela vyřazeno z provozu. Kvůli útoku dronů hořelo také na letišti v ruském černomořském letovisku Soči.
Mezi čtyřmi raněnými v Dnipru jsou dvě osmileté dívky, jedna je v péči lékařů v nemocnici, napsal na sociální síti náčelník tamní regionální vojenské správy Oleksandr Hanža. Ruská vojska během noci také opět zaútočila na Oděsu na…

titulek: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 15 people
titulekPuvodni: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 15 people
shrnuti: Volodymyr Zelensky says the attack, which left children dead, was Russia expressing its "thanks" for a US diesel deal.

vyrez.text:
Ukraine war: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 15 people - BBC News
Image source, Reuters
By Vitaly Shevchenko   and   Tom McArthur
Published
10 October 2026, 11:29 BST
Updated 1 hour ago
Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 15 people including three children, officials said.
The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the south-eastern city on Saturday morning. At least 16 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.
He added that 13 other regions had come under attack overnight, arguing this demonstrated Russia took "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting".
Photos and videos from the site of one of the strikes in Zaporizhzhia show an apartment block mostly destroyed.
"The ground floor was hit, and the floors above just collapsed," acting Mayor Regina Kharchenko told Ukrainian television from the scene.

Obyvatelé ukrajinského Kramatorsku se naučili žít pod neustálou hrozbou ruských útoků, popsala v Interview ČT24 zahraniční zpravodajka ČT Darja Stomatová. Kvůli dronům se lidé po městě často pohybují pěšky, aby se v případě nebezpečí mohli rychle ukrýt. Navzdory pokračujícímu ostřelování zde stále fungují obchody, tržiště i kavárny. Russian jet-powered drone shot down near Lviv after entering city | Ukrainska Pravda
A jet-powered drone. Photo: RIA Novosti
Air defence forces have shot down a Russian jet-powered drone near the city of Lviv after it flew into the city on the morning of 10 October.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force ; Lviv Mayor Andrii Sadovyi ; Maksym Kozytskyi , Head of Lviv Oblast Military Administration
Details: At 07:19, the Air Force reported a jet-powered UAV heading towards Vynnyky and Lviv. The military later added that the drone was flying towards Lviv airport.
Advertisement:





At almost the same time, Sadovyi reported a Russian drone heading towards the city. At 07:23, he said it had entered the airspace over Lviv.
Kozytskyi reported that air defence forces were responding and later wrote that the drone had been destroyed near Lviv. Early reports indicate that there are no casualties or damage.
Thus, the Air Force and local authorities were reporting on the same drone, with the military explicitly describing it as jet-powered.
This is the first known instance of a Russian jet-powered UAV entering directly into Lviv's airspace.

Zelenskyy furious as Trump announces deal to buy Russian diesel
President says deal essential to lower US fuel prices but move set to create fresh crisis with Ukraine and Nato allies
US politics – live updates
Donald Trump was on a fresh collision course with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and European allies on Friday after a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its four-and-a-half year war against Ukraine.
Zelenskyy reacted furiously to Trump’s announcement of the deal with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, calling it “absolutely terrible” and “not fair and not honest”.

Zelenskyy condemns US decision to allow Russian diesel imports | Ukrainska Pravda
Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Photo: Getty Images
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that US President Donald Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russia and allow it to export diesel fuel is a birthday present for Vladimir Putin.
Source: Zelenskyy in a telephone interview with Axios
Details: Zelenskyy expressed disappointment, saying Trump's actions look "absolutely terrible" . He said such bilateral agreements will provide Russia with additional funds that will be used entirely to wage war.
Advertisement:





Quote: "You know, it looks like a happy birthday present for Putin. It looks absolutely terrible."
Details: Zelenskyy stressed that the decision gives Putin more resources and enables him to wage war even more aggressively.
Quote: "At precisely the moment when we are talking about peace, America is allowing Russia to export diesel. We are talking about millions, billions [of dollars]. In any case, all this money goes towards the war."
Background:
On the evening of 9 October, Trump said he had spoken by phone with Putin and agreed on supplies of millions of tonnes of Russian diesel…
